title: Choose the visual world for Photnoo
question: Every direction keeps the PHOTNO logo and the green. Keep the lead direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Private View
options.lineage: White-cube photography exhibitions and their wall-text systems
options.thesis: Every delivery is a private view: the gallery is hung, the invitation carries the password, and the exhibition runs seven days.
options.viewport: A deep-green wall with three large client photographs hung at eye level and museum placards; the headline set as exhibition wall text; primary action Request access placed like the room's entry sign.
options.risk: Can drift into austere and slow if the wall text replaces clear product copy.

raised.raise: Green is laid as whole flat wall fields per room, never scattered accents.
States print themselves as wall-text lines (Shared, 5 days left) instead of pill badges.
Every photo keeps its provenance placard visible: file, size, downloaded by, when.
Allowance and days left read as a measured fill line on the wall, a physical gauge.
The visitor book (proof of views and downloads) stacks newest on top, older entries fade.
Two inks only: green and one brass picture-light accent; nothing else gets color.

options.label: Lay-flat Album
options.lineage: Premium lay-flat wedding albums and photography monographs
options.thesis: The product is the album the client keeps: green book cloth, foil-stamped star, full-bleed spreads.
options.viewport: A cloth-bound album cover open onto a full-bleed spread, with the headline foil-stamped on the cover and Request access as a ribbon marker.
options.risk: The familiar premium-photography direction most runs land on; risks reading as a wedding-album vendor.

options.label: Solidarity Silkscreen
options.thesis: Flat fearless color fields around one emblem, the slogan repeated in four languages.
options.viewport: One emblem centered, multilingual slogan border.
options.risk: Posters compete with the photographers' own photos.
options.case: Fuses poorly: photographers do not see their work in protest posters, and the loud fields bury the photos.
options.kept: Total color commitment: green owns whole regions.

options.label: Sticker Accretion
options.thesis: Layered, half-covered stickers as a record of time.
options.risk: Nothing is fully legible, the opposite of premium delivery.
options.case: Fuses poorly: illegibility fights the client flow and the brand.
options.kept: Chronology as depth for the activity log.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.thesis: Every block seamed to its owner, date and history.
options.viewport: An unequal patch grid with cloth labels.
options.risk: Domestic craft reads homemade, not premium studio.
options.case: Fuses partly on family memories, loses on product clarity.

options.label: Glaze River Shelf
options.thesis: Molten color that runs, stops and pools.
options.viewport: A row of glazed cups with recipe cards.
options.risk: Ceramics has nothing to do with photography.
options.case: Fuses poorly on audience; the threshold idea survives.
options.kept: Allowance and expiry as physical fill levels.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: One continuous transcript, states print themselves.
options.risk: Cold and technical for clients opening wedding photos.
options.case: Fuses poorly: clients are non-technical; green matches but tone does not.
options.kept: States as printed lines, not chrome.

options.label: Risograph System
options.thesis: Two spot inks misregistered over grain.
options.risk: Zine energy undercuts a paid professional tool.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful print culture, not studio delivery.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS landing like Pixieset or Pic-Time, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Left headline and CTA, right a product screenshot of a client gallery, logo strip, feature grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
